drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Here is the scenario. A retail group spends heavily on Claude.
drills.answer_line: SAM: The answer is B. A gateway with aliases
drills.stem: The finance director wants to buy a GPU cluster, self-host Kimi K3.1 Pro and move all traffic off Claude. Traffic is bursty, there is no sovereignty requirement, and nobody runs model inference today. What should the architect recommend?

options.A: Self-host Kimi on a new cluster and move all traffic
options.B: Gateway with model aliases: simple high-volume tasks to a hosted open-weight model, frontier model for hard steps, each route settled by an eval
options.C: Stay entirely on Claude, because open models are not at frontier quality
options.D: Run one small Apache-licensed model on a single server for all traffic

drills.why: No sovereignty need and bursty traffic: route, do not self-host. A buys a multi-server cluster nobody can run, C ignores the cost lever asked about, D trades quality for licence neatness.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. An inference platform resells model access
drills.answer_line: SAM: A is right. D is modified M I T
drills.stem: Choose two. An inference platform resells model access by the token, revenue well above $20M a year, and wants open models it can serve without a separate agreement with the maker. Going by the licences as reported, which two qualify?
drills.why: Gemma 4 and gpt-oss are Apache 2.0. Kimi needs an agreement for cloud resale above the threshold, Mistral Large 4's modified MIT needs a reseller deal, Muse Spark Open has a separate deal for large MaaS providers.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A utilities company's inspectors
drills.answer_line: SAM: The queue covers the gaps by not summarising during them
drills.stem: Inspectors work in tunnels with no signal for hours and want notes summarised on the tablet as they type; notes may not leave the device until it docks. Which approach fits?

options.A: Claude Haiku through the API, queuing requests until the tablet reconnects
options.B: A small Gemma 4 model running on the tablet
options.C: Claude through Bedrock in the nearest region
options.D: Kimi K3.1 Pro self-hosted at the depot

drills.why: No network is the constraint and Claude has no offline option. A summarises only after reconnecting, C is still a cloud, D needs a cluster.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false.
drills.answer_line: SAM: All four. One: federal civilian agencies only
drills.prompt: True or false? 1) The DHS order bars all US companies from using DeepSeek. 2) The order reaches third-party products built on DeepSeek technology. 3) A federal contractor ban on Kimi is law today. 4) A coding tool's own model can be built on Chinese open weights without the base model appearing in its name.
drills.answer: 1) False: federal civilian agencies only, exceptions on request. 2) True. 3) False: proposed, not enacted. 4) True: Cursor's Composer 2 on Kimi K2.5 (per Menlo).

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A media company is trialling the Grok A P I
drills.answer_line: SAM: A and B. A stops a silent model change
drills.stem: Choose two. A media company is trialling the Grok API for an internal research assistant. Which two controls address the documented risks?

options.A: Pin a dated model ID in production instead of the latest alias
options.B: Require evidence of xAI's change management for model and system-prompt changes, plus audit reports under NDA
options.C: Block the trial until Ofcom and the European Commission publish findings
options.D: Accept the vendor's statement that business data is not used for training
options.E: Use only the image-generation product, since the investigations covered text

drills.why: A stops silent model changes; B tests the control that failed at least twice in 2025. C waits on probes into a different product, D is unverified, E has it backwards.

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the four segments
drills.answer_line: ALEX: What open weights buy, with the licence.
drills.prompt: Name the four segments, and the question you would ask the customer in each.
drills.answer: What open weights buy and the licence; self-hosting and sovereignty; provenance; xAI. Behind for which task; cost or control; what are your vendors' models built on; who approves changes.

In this episode: What open weights give that Claude cannot
Licence drift: what open still allows
Factual risk questions on xAI's Grok
Cold open: the self-hosting proposal: Proposal: self-host the strongest open model
Segment one: what open weights buy: Open weights: the model layer only
Chinese models 89% of open-model spend (Menlo, an Anthropic investor)
Best open model ~20 points behind the leader on the AA index
Open: 19% of enterprise tokens, 4% of spend
Strengths: runs anywhere, post-trainable, cheap per token
Flagships drifted to custom licences; resale often restricted
Segment two: self-hosting cost and sover: Inference options: lab API, hosted provider, cloud marketplace, own GPUs
Frontier open models need several servers
Hidden costs: idle GPUs, ops staff, evals, migrations
91% of post-training companies use outside partners
Self-host pays: sustained volume or hard control rule
Residency is where data is processed; sovereignty is who operates it
Segment three: provenance and procuremen: Where inference runs differs from where weights came from
DHS order: DeepSeek out of federal civilian agencies
Order covers third-party products built on DeepSeek
Kimi, Qwen, GLM: proposals, not law
Weights hide inside products; keep a model bill of materials
Segment four: xAI and Grok: SpaceX reportedly owns xAI; closed its Cursor purchase in August
Strengths: lower token price, wide distribution, federal deal
AA index: Grok 4.7 below the best open-weight model
2025 output incidents; 2026 image probes, no findings yet
Probes target the consumer product, not the API
Ask: change management, pinned versions, audit reports
Cold open: the verdict: Answer: B, route through a gateway with evals
A: cluster for bursty traffic, nobody to run it
C: ignores the cost lever asked about
D: quality traded for licence neatness
Five to remember: Open weights: offline, post-training, price; trail the frontier
"Open" is not a licence; permissive tier is small and mid models
Self-host for sustained volume or a hard control rule
Residency, sovereignty, provenance; model bill of materials
Grok: pin a version, demand change evidence, verify claims
Recap: the conversation tells: "Open models are behind" → behind for which task?
"It's open source" → use inside or resell? Read the licence
"Self-host to save money" → utilisation and who runs it
"No outside party may touch the data" → self-host or on-device
"Sovereign" → where data sits, or who operates it?
"No DeepSeek" → what are your vendors' models built on?
"Is Grok safe?" → which product, which pinned version, who approves changes
